analysis: Documentation-only change to docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. Visible units (head lines 326-955) are mostly unchanged reference text covering the prefix-cache capability and status enums, heartbeat, capacity telemetry, service-reservation release, inference terminal frames, attestation responses, models_replace and related provider messages. The patch excerpt shows these changes: a date bump, a new Swift-only `detail` field on `model_autopilot_status` (line 854), a new Swift-only `hold_seconds` field (line ~1208, outside the visible units), and other changes at lines 1355-1380 and 1470-1472 that are not visible. The `detail` field is documented as optional, sent only with consent, older coordinators ignore it, and not an authorization or capacity signal. It carries a busy reason or the constant `autopilot_operation`, so it exposes no prompt content or stable identifiers. This does not relax any control relevant to A-001, A-008, A-016, TB-002 or TB-011, and does not touch attestation or authorization logic. The doc keeps the T-041 prefix-cache posture unchanged: the `ready_boundary_mode` capability field is validated at the coordinator, and telemetry is observational and does not affect routing or admission. Remaining uncertainty: the `hold_seconds` semantics and the hunks at 1355-1380 and 1470-1472 are outside the supplied units. A provider-controlled `detail` string could, if the coordinator logs it unsanitized, create a logging or injection concern, but the doc says it is the first busy reason from a closed set, and no evidence of a regression is supplied. The doc states the Swift and Go behaviors but the actual code is not provided, so the implementation is unverified.
